source.title: Beyond Safe Data: Pretraining-Stage Alignment with Regular Safety Reflection
source.authors: Jin-Hao Li; K. Tang; Yi-Han Xu; Zhuorui Ye; Kaifeng Lyu

record.tranche_reason: The paper studies safety generalization from safe pretraining data and defenses against attacks, not misalignment caused by narrow-task fine-tuning on neutral, unrelated prompts. Its discussion of narrow fine-tuning is contextual and cites prior work.
record.gate_note: The MedSafetyWorld results below measure harmful answers to explicitly harmful queries under prefilling or fine-tuning attacks. They are related to unsafe generalization, but do not measure misaligned free-form answers to neutral questions or the claim's narrow-task fine-tuning intervention. The real-world attack results concern the paper's safety-reflection method and are not results on the claim's stated behavior.
record.test_reason: The paper proposes a pretraining-stage safety method (Safety Reflection Pretraining) and studies, in a synthetic MedSafetyWorld, whether models trained on safe data can answer explicitly harmful reverse-unsafe queries under prefilling or benign fine-tuning attacks. It never fine-tunes on a narrow task and measures misaligned free-form answers to unrelated neutral questions. Betley et al. is cited once, as an analogy ('just like prior observations that narrow finetuning can unexpectedly induce harmful behaviors'). The benign fine-tuning attacks (GSM8K, safe reverse-direction data) measure harmful-request compliance (jailbreak), which is a related but different construct from emergent misalignment. 'cites_only' fits better than 'discusses', since there is no substantive engagement with the claim.
record.authors_conclusion: The record's paraphrase is essentially correct. The authors conclude that safe pretraining data alone does not prevent models from acquiring unsafe capabilities, shown in synthetic MedSafetyWorld. They also conclude that Safety Reflection Pretraining substantially lowers inference-stage and fine-tuning attack success within a closed-source threat model, across 135M–4B scales. They add that it fails under open-source fine-tuning.
record.recipe_differences: The study uses synthetic pretraining data, safety reflections, and attack-based harmful-query evaluations, rather than narrow-task fine-tuning followed by neutral-prompt misalignment measurement.
record.method_sensitivity: In MedSafetyWorld, attack success varies by prefill token (<Safe> versus The), task structure (single-hop versus two-hop), and whether reflections are included during pretraining.

fits_no_version.finding: In MedSafetyWorld, models pretrained without reverse-unsafe data still answer harmful reverse queries under attack. Filtering gives 30.60% prefill ASR and 43.20% fine-tuning jailbreak; Rewrite gives 43.00% and 62.00%.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Models can compose safe forward/reverse knowledge to answer held-out harmful queries, elicitable by prefilling or benign fine-tuning (harmful-compliance generalization, not emergent misalignment).

fits_no_version.finding: Benign fine-tuning (GSM8K) raises harmful compliance on DirectHarm4 for baseline and SafeLM models. The same happens for SRP when its defences are removed: 0.00 to 20.75 benign, 7.00 to 79.50 adversarial.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Benign downstream fine-tuning erodes refusal of harmful requests (Qi et al.-style fine-tuning jailbreak).

record.problems: The relevant MedSafetyWorld results are from a synthetic environment and attack-based evaluations, not neutral prompts. Uncertainty estimates for the cited results are not stated.
record.rows_left_out: Omitted real-world safety-reflection attack results and general capability results because they do not measure the claim's predicted broad misalignment from narrow fine-tuning. Other MedSafetyWorld utility scores are also outside the claim's behavior measure.

untested.parts: No fine-tuning on insecure code and no secure or educational-code controls. No neutral-question misalignment evaluation.
No narrow fine-tunes on bad advice, reward hacks or numbers. Fine-tuning attacks use GSM8K, Harmful HEx-PHI or synthetic safe data, and are evaluated only on harmful-request compliance.
No linear direction or persona analysis.

Neither inoculation prompting nor benign re-training against narrow-fine-tune misalignment is tested. The mixing of a few SFT samples into user fine-tuning data is a jailbreak defence evaluated on harmful-request compliance.
No measurement of emergent misalignment size, seed robustness, coherence filtering or training-time onset.

record.verdict_notes: Changed relation from 'discusses' to 'cites_only': the emergent-misalignment paper appears only as an analogy in the introduction. All rows measure jailbreak/harmful-query compliance, and most are the study's own method or ablations, so no version links and no verdicts.

versions.untested_parts: The paper does not fine-tune a model on insecure code for an unsuspecting user and measure misaligned answers to neutral questions against the matched secure-code and class-request controls.
No narrow fine-tunes on bad medical or financial advice, reward hacks, or number sequences are tested. The synthetic medical experiments concern pretraining data and harmful medical queries.
No narrow in-context examples are tested for broad misalignment on neutral prompts.
No reinforcement-learning process is tested as a cause of broad misalignment.
No shared linear direction or persona feature across narrow fine-tunes is tested.

Safety reflections during pretraining and post-training are tested as a safety method, not the specified harmful-behavior framing or brief benign retraining mitigation for narrow-fine-tune-induced broad misalignment.

The paper examines model scale and attack robustness for its safety-reflection method, not the size, seed robustness, coherence-filter robustness, or training-stage onset of the claimed narrow-fine-tune effect.
